# Building surfaces and solids

These layers build geometry from a model, a function, a field or a
shape. This article gives a small example of each. Installation is
covered in [Get
started](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/ggplot3d.md).
[Choosing layers for observations and
grids](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/layers.md) covers
points, paths, surfaces from gridded data, columns, distributions and
intervals. [Drawing arrows and
streamlines](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/vector-fields.md)
covers arrows and streamlines, and [Constructing and reconstructing
surfaces](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/implicit-surfaces.md)
covers reconstruction from point clouds.

``` r

library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)
```

## Indexed meshes

A mesh describes vertices and faces using integer indices. Indices start
at one. Each row in the face matrix identifies the corners of a triangle
or quadrilateral. The mesh constructor returns a corner table keyed by
vertex, face and corner.

``` r

vertices <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 1, 0), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
                       z = c(0, 0, 1, 1))
mesh <- mesh_3d(vertices, matrix(1:4, nrow = 1))
ggplot() + geom_mesh_3d(data = mesh, fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Function and fitted surfaces

Function surfaces sample a vectorized function of x and y. The grid is
evenly spaced in transformed x and y coordinates. Function inputs and
returned z values use original data units. The z scale transforms the
returned heights.

``` r

ggplot() + geom_function_3d(fun = function(x, y) sin(x) * cos(y), n = 10) +
  xlim(-2, 2) + ylim(-2, 2) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

ggplot() + stat_function_3d(fun = function(x, y) x^2 + y^2, n = 10) +
  xlim(-1, 1) + ylim(-1, 1) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Fitted surfaces model z using x and y. Fitting and prediction use
transformed positions. The linear model’s default formula is z as a
function of x plus y. Confidence surfaces, when requested, describe
pointwise uncertainty in the conditional mean.

``` r

fit_data <- expand.grid(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 10),
                        y = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 10))
fit_data$z <- with(fit_data, x + y + sin(3 * x * y) / 5)
f <- ggplot(fit_data, aes(x, y, z = z))
f + geom_smooth_3d(method = "lm", se = FALSE, n = 8) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

f + stat_smooth_3d(method = "lm", se = FALSE, n = 8) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

An existing model can supply predictions directly. Fit fuel consumption
against weight and horsepower, then pass that model to both the surface
and residual layers. The hull domain ends the surface at the convex hull
of the observed x/y positions; residual segments join observations to
predictions.

``` r

model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
cars_fit <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, hp, z = mpg))
cars_fit + geom_smooth_3d(method = model, domain = "hull", se = FALSE,
                         n = 10, fill = "#2E6F9E", alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_residual_3d(method = model, colour = "#B5342B", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 1.5) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Models supplied as objects predict in original data units. Fitting
functions, including custom functions passed as the method, fit
transformed positions and use a formula in x, y and z. A model with
additional predictors can fix them through the condition list; see
[geom_smooth_3d()](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_smooth_3d.md).

Colour can show prediction standard errors on the fitted surface.
Confidence bounds can also be drawn as separate surfaces or a closed
band. They describe pointwise uncertainty in the fitted mean.

``` r

cars_fit + geom_smooth_3d(method = model, domain = "hull", se = "fill", n = 10) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#DCEAF3", high = "#2E6F9E", name = "SE") +
  coord_3d() + theme(legend.position = "right")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Use `se = "band"` to close the space between the confidence surfaces.
The following band uses the same fitted model and predictor hull.

``` r

cars_fit + geom_smooth_3d(method = model, domain = "hull", se = "band",
                         n = 10, fill = "#2E6F9E", alpha = 0.45) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 1.5) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

[Displaying intervals and
summaries](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/intervals.md)
covers supplied intervals and summaries of repeated observations.

## Parametric surfaces

A parametric surface gives x, y and z as functions of two parameters
$`u`$ and $`v`$, which reaches shapes that are not graphs of a function
of x and y.
[`geom_parametric_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_parametric_3d.md)
takes a function returning a list of the three coordinates and samples
it on an `n` grid; `closed` joins the edges of a parameter that wraps
around, as both do for a torus.

``` r

torus <- function(u, v) list(x = (1 + 0.4 * cos(v)) * cos(u),
                             y = (1 + 0.4 * cos(v)) * sin(u), z = 0.4 * sin(v))
ggplot() +
  geom_parametric_3d(fun = torus, n = c(36, 18), closed = TRUE, fill = "#2E6F9E") +
  coord_3d(aspect = "data")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

[Reading and measuring
meshes](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/meshes.html#geodesics-on-a-parametric-surface)
draws geodesics on this torus, and [Drawing complex functions, knots and
surfaces](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/complex-knots.md)
uses parametric surfaces that pass through themselves.

## Density surfaces and ridges

A bivariate density surface estimates how observations are distributed
over x and y. Its height is density, computed with a Gaussian product
kernel. The bandwidth controls smoothing along each input axis.

``` r

ggplot(faithful, aes(eruptions, waiting)) +
  stat_density_2d_3d(n = 12) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Ridgelines estimate a one-dimensional density for each group and place
the groups along the perpendicular axis. Here each species occupies a
single y position. Height multiplies the density in transformed z units.

``` r

r <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, as.numeric(Species),
                     group = Species, fill = Species))
r + geom_ridgeline_3d(n = 24) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2E6F9E", "#9E5E0F", "#2A7A7A")) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

r + stat_ridgeline_3d(n = 24) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2E6F9E", "#9E5E0F", "#2A7A7A")) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Scalar-field level surfaces

A scalar field assigns a numeric value to each x/y/z position. An
isosurface joins positions with the same field value. Supply a complete
rectilinear grid and map the field to `value`; missing field values mask
their incident cells.

``` r

field <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8),
  y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8), z = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8))
field$value <- with(field, x^2 + y^2 + z^2)
v <- ggplot(field, aes(x, y, z = z, value = value))
v + geom_isosurface_3d(levels = 0.6, fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

v + stat_isosurface_3d(levels = 0.6, fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

A function can supply field values directly. It receives transformed
coordinates in all three axes. Grid resolution sets how finely the
function is sampled.

``` r

ball <- function(x, y, z) x^2 + y^2 + z^2
ggplot() + geom_isofunction_3d(fun = ball, n = 8, levels = 0.5) +
  xlim(-1, 1) + ylim(-1, 1) + zlim(-1, 1) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

ggplot() + stat_isofunction_3d(fun = ball, n = 8, levels = 0.5) +
  xlim(-1, 1) + ylim(-1, 1) + zlim(-1, 1) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Slices through a scalar field

A level surface shows where a field takes one value. A slice shows every
value on a plane through it.
[`geom_slice_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_slice_3d.md)
reads a gridded field with a `value` aesthetic and colours planes
through it, by default the three planes through the middle of the grid;
`xslice`, `yslice` and `zslice` choose others.
[`geom_slice_contour_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_slice_contour_3d.md)
adds contour lines on the same planes.

``` r

field <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 16),
                     y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 16),
                     z = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 16))
field$value <- with(field, exp(-(x^2 + 2 * y^2 + z^2)))
ggplot(field, aes(x, y, z = z, value = value)) +
  geom_slice_3d(zslice = 0) +
  geom_slice_contour_3d(zslice = 0, bins = 6, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#C9D9E6", high = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

`stat_slice_3d(slice = sdf_plane(...))` cuts along an oblique plane, and
[`geom_density_slice_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_slice_3d.md)
slices the density of a point cloud estimated on the fly.

[Slicing fields and point
densities](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/articles/field-slices.md)
works through both operations, with grid checks, missing values and
bandwidth comparisons.

## Where two surfaces meet

[`geom_isocurve_3d()`](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_isocurve_3d.md)
draws the curve where two implicit surfaces intersect, the points at
which both functions are zero. Here a unit sphere meets a saddle.

``` r

ggplot() +
  geom_isocurve_3d(fun1 = sdf_sphere(radius = 1),
                   fun2 = function(x, y, z) x^2 - y^2 - z * 0.5,
                   n = 24, colour = "#B5342B", linewidth = 1) +
  xlim(-1.2, 1.2) + ylim(-1.2, 1.2) + zlim(-1.2, 1.2) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Trivariate density

A trivariate density estimates the distribution of observations in three
dimensions. Numeric levels select density thresholds. Probability
contents, given as `probs`, select enclosed mass estimated from the
sampled grid. The grid ranges need to include the density tails for
probability-content requests.

``` r

set.seed(4)
cloud <- data.frame(x = rnorm(40), y = rnorm(40), z = rnorm(40))
c <- ggplot(cloud, aes(x, y, z = z))
c + geom_isodensity_3d(h = 0.7, levels = 0.02, n = 8) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

c + stat_density_3d(h = 0.7, levels = 0.02, n = 8) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

ggplot(cloud, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  stat_density_3d(h = 0.7, probs = c(0.5, 0.9), n = 12, alpha = 0.4) +
  xlim(-4, 4) + ylim(-4, 4) + scale_z_continuous(limits = c(-4, 4)) + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Convex hulls

A convex hull is the smallest convex shape containing the input
positions. This example uses the eight corners of a cube. Coplanar input
produces a planar polygon, and collinear input produces no faces.

``` r

corners <- expand.grid(x = 0:1, y = 0:1, z = 0:1)
h <- ggplot(corners, aes(x, y, z = z))
h + geom_hull_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

h + stat_hull_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Spheres, ellipsoids and glyphs

A sphere gives each observation a solid radius. The next table contains
three centres and radii in data units. A data aspect ratio makes equal
distances on the axes equally long in the scene.

``` r

solids <- data.frame(x = c(0, 2, 4), y = c(0, 1, 0), z = c(0, 1, 2),
                     radius = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.6))
ggplot(solids, aes(x, y, z = z, radius = radius)) +
  geom_sphere_3d(detail = 1, fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d(aspect = "data")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

An ellipsoid takes three semi-axis lengths or a list-column of shape
matrices. These lengths use transformed position units. Principal axes
are visible through a translucent ellipsoid.

``` r

ggplot(solids, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_ellipsoid_3d(rx = 0.7, ry = 0.3, rz = 0.5, detail = 1,
                    axes = TRUE, alpha = 0.4, fill = "#2A7A7A") +
  coord_3d(aspect = "data")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ellipsoid stat estimates a shape from each group. In the iris data,
a data ellipsoid describes the spread of flower measurements. A
confidence ellipsoid describes uncertainty in the species mean; choose
it with the standard-error kind and a normal covariance estimate.

``` r

iris_space <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, Sepal.Width, z = Petal.Length,
                               fill = Species, colour = Species))
iris_space + stat_ellipsoid_3d(type = "norm", kind = "data",
                              detail = 1, alpha = 0.2, axes = TRUE) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2E6F9E", "#9E5E0F", "#2A7A7A")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2E6F9E", "#9E5E0F", "#2A7A7A")) +
  coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

``` r

iris_space + stat_ellipsoid_3d(type = "norm", kind = "se", level = 0.95,
                              detail = 1, alpha = 0.4, axes = TRUE) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#2E6F9E", "#9E5E0F", "#2A7A7A")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2E6F9E", "#9E5E0F", "#2A7A7A")) +
  coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

[stat_ellipsoid_3d()](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_ellipsoid_3d.md)
also offers a t estimate that downweights outliers, Euclidean spheres
and enclosing ellipsoids. Each group needs four or more points spanning
three dimensions.

A glyph places a mesh at every observation. Built-in shapes include
cubes, cones, cylinders, spheres and octahedra; a custom mesh can supply
another shape. Here the cube width represents horsepower in the car
data, with width measured in millimetres at the centre of the view.

``` r

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, z = qsec, size = hp)) +
  geom_glyph_3d(glyph = "cube", fill = "#9E5E0F") + coord_3d()
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## Tubes, strips and sweeps

A tube gives a path thickness in transformed data units. Sample a helix
in row order and map radius to widen it gradually. Its circular
cross-section follows the curve with a rotation-minimising frame, which
controls its orientation along the path.

``` r

angle <- seq(0, 3 * pi, length.out = 40)
helix <- data.frame(x = cos(angle), y = sin(angle), z = angle / 4,
                    radius = seq(0.05, 0.14, length.out = length(angle)))
curve <- ggplot(helix, aes(x, y, z = z))
curve + geom_tube_3d(aes(radius = radius), sides = 8, cap = "flat",
                     fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d(aspect = "data")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

A radius in data units stretches with the panel box. With
`radius.unit = "mm"` the radius is measured on the page instead, like a
line width, so the tube stays round on screen in a box three times as
wide as it is deep.

``` r

curve + geom_tube_3d(radius = 1.5, radius.unit = "mm", fill = "#2E6F9E") +
  coord_3d(aspect = c(3, 1, 1.6))
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

A strip sweeps a line segment along the same path. Its width and twist
can vary at each position; twist is measured in degrees. The normal
argument sets the initial orientation.

``` r

curve + geom_strip_3d(aes(twist = z * 60), width = 0.35,
                       normal = c(0, 0, 1), fill = "#9E5E0F") +
  coord_3d(aspect = "data")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Supply a two-column polygon to sweep another cross-section. Its radius
parameter scales the profile. Closed paths can close the seam, and a
spline can interpolate a sparse set of path points before the sweep.

``` r

route <- data.frame(x = 0:4, y = c(0, 1, 0, -1, 0), z = c(0, 0.3, 1, 1.2, 2))
square <- rbind(c(-1, -1), c(1, -1), c(1, 1), c(-1, 1))
ggplot(route, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_sweep_3d(profile = square, radius = 0.15, spline = "natural", n = 32,
                fill = "#2A7A7A") + coord_3d(aspect = "data")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

To draw the smooth path itself, use
[stat_spline_3d()](https://gillescolling.com/ggplot3d/reference/stat_spline_3d.md).
A surface of revolution rotates a radius-height profile about an axis.

``` r

vessel <- data.frame(z = seq(0, 2, length.out = 16))
vessel$r <- 0.5 + 0.2 * sin(3 * vessel$z)
ggplot(vessel, aes(r = r, z = z)) +
  geom_revolve_3d(n = 16, fill = "#7A4F9E") + coord_3d(aspect = "data")
```

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)
